correctness.rationale: The ten arcs i→i+1,i+2 on Z/5 give 901 non-strong-connectivity subsets (face vector including empty 1,10,45,120,210,250,185,70,10). Independently enumerated all 1024 arc masks and greedily matched faces in the stated order (8,2,5,9,7,1,6,0,4,3): exactly 450 reduced pairs, sole remaining bitmask 189 (six vertices); removing the empty↔vertex-8 pair leaves one critical vertex and one 5-face. Independently built the whole 900-node oriented nonempty Hasse graph and topologically sorted every vertex; an acyclic Morse CW complex with one 0- and one 5-cell is S^5. For every nonidentity element of C5 the arc orbits are full directed Hamiltonian 5-cycles; no simplex may have invariant support, proving free action on the geometric realization (not just on arc vertices). This simply connected sphere universal-cover argument gives quotient pi1=H1=Z/5, and transfer yields rational sphere homology; top degree action on Q must be +1 since it has odd order. All objects are spanning directed subgraphs with reachability defined on the five labelled vertices.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Hultman 2004 Theorem 4.1 imposes 2-dense cycles with directed 2-cycles; a tournament has none. Classical complexes of all directed edges have a different ambient arc set, so a general sphere-wedge statement for those objects does not imply this exact specialized C5 action.
